subtopic: Blamed for something I did not do
passage: Mridul, you look tense. Let me tell you what I did at ten. I am Eshaan, your Mama. A window in our school broke during cricket, and it was my shot. When the headmaster asked, my friend Bhairavi was standing next to me, and I said nothing. She got a week of lunches in the office. I felt sick every night; I could not enjoy my dal. On Monday my knees shook, but I walked to my teacher and told her it was me. Then I found Bhairavi and said sorry. She was angry for a few days. The fear passed in an hour, and the regret would have stayed with me.

qa.q: Why could Eshaan not enjoy his dal?
qa.a: He felt sick and guilty for letting Bhairavi take the blame.

qa.q: What did Eshaan do that fixed part of the problem?
qa.a: He went to his teacher, told her the truth, and then apologised to Bhairavi.

qa.q: How might Bhairavi have felt when Eshaan first said nothing?
qa.a: Bhairavi probably felt let down and unfairly punished, and that is likely why she stayed angry for a few days.

grounding: An elder recalls letting a friend take the blame out of fear, feeling sick, then admitting the truth to the teacher and apologising.
